html:
A Moroccan scholar from Tangier who spent about thirty years travelling across Africa, Asia and Europe, some 117,000 kilometres by his own account. He told his story in a book known as the Rihla, "The Journey".

He set out in 1325, aged 21, for the pilgrimage to Mecca, and kept going. He crossed Egypt, Syria, Iraq and Persia, sailed down the coast of the Swahili cities of East Africa, and rode across the steppes of the Golden Horde. In India he reached Delhi and served the sultan of the Delhi Sultanate as a judge for years. He went on to the Maldives, Sri Lanka, Bengal and Sumatra, and says he reached China under the Yuan.

Back home in 1349, he soon set out again, to Spain and then across the Sahara from Sijilmasa to visit Mali in 1352 and 1353. The sultan of Morocco had a scholar write down his memories. Some passages seem borrowed from other writers, but the book is a rare picture of the 14th century Muslim world, which stretched almost everywhere he went.
sum: A Moroccan scholar from Tangier who spent about thirty years travelling across Africa, Asia and Europe, some 117,000 kilometres by his own account. He told his story in a book known as the Rihla, "The Journey".
